matching: Use each document rendering's public blocks count as the target. Fit the two semantic thresholds independently from that rendering's eligible sibling cosine scores. Choose the nearest attainable count, preferring fewer passages on a tie and then the lowest cutoff partition. The finite-cap search evaluates distinct partitions in cutoff order until it finds an exact match or exhausts them. Verify each chosen layout against the public chunker. Only source text and passage count enter selection.
retrieval: Return each ranked passage in full. The principal measure is complete annotated evidence in the union of the first five dense hits. Also score the whole first hit, fractional evidence recall at both ranks, and the actual tokens in the returned texts including separators. Search the original candidate pools. Index every emitted passage and use the same encoder for the three indexes.
inference: Use the previously reported 1,266 confirmation questions and replay the 1,122 development questions. Average the three public-service renderings within question and give the four domains equal weight. Use 4,000 paired bootstrap resamples of page families, publishers, issuers and papers. Report 98.33% intervals for the three primary top-five comparisons and descriptive 95% intervals for top-one. An exact-count sensitivity requires multiple passages and equal counts for all three methods in every rendering of the query source, retaining the original candidate pools.
